card: Stops chain verification from falsely reporting database corruption when startup checks or verifychain encounter missing undo data on refetched pruned blocks or AssumeUTXO snapshot chainstates. Using getblockfrompeer downloads a pruned block body without undo data, causing verification at level 3 or 4 to treat missing undo records as database corruption and prevent the node from starting. The fix treats missing undo data as unavailable history, returning incomplete verification status rather than aborting. This bug was found during review of pruned txindex (#36002) and unblocks pending pruneassumevalid changes.
changed_since_previous: The previous description was generated without a patch; this version confirms the implementation in CVerifyDB::VerifyDB and the addition of functional regression tests for AssumeUTXO snapshots and getblockfrompeer.
evidence: PR description: 'getblockfrompeer restores a pruned block\'s body without recreating its undo record. If startup verification reaches that block at level >2, it attempts to disconnect it and reports database corruption, preventing the node from restarting.'
PR description notes it arose during pruned txindex review (#36002) and is required for pending pruneassumevalid work.
problem: Refetching a pruned block via getblockfrompeer restores the block body but not its undo data. When startup checks or the verifychain RPC run at check level 3 or higher, the node attempts to disconnect blocks to verify UTXO manipulation, encounters missing undo records, falsely reports database corruption, and aborts startup.

risk.why: A mistake in CVerifyDB could prematurely stop verification of actually corrupted chainstates during node startup or verifychain calls.

summary: Stops chain verification in CVerifyDB::VerifyDB early when deep verification checks encounter missing block undo data on pruned nodes or AssumeUTXO snapshot chainstates. Missing undo data is treated as unavailable history rather than a database corruption failure, returning an incomplete verification status. This allows nodes to restart cleanly and run verifychain even if pruned blocks have been refetched without undo records.
